calls.summary: Margaret Ellison called after reading about Genesis AI rechargeable aids and mentioned lifelong tinnitus that keeps her up at night. Agent Oscar explained the platform's tinnitus relief features and Edge Mode+, then booked her for an in-clinic consultation and online hearing test. Margaret confirmed the appointment and asked for directions to the Eden Prairie provider.

Robert Hensley wanted a second opinion after reading an Edge AI review online and asked whether the new platform was truly made in the USA. Agent Lila confirmed the Minnesota manufacturing and walked him through fall detection and Bluetooth streaming. She scheduled a consultation with a nearby provider and Robert agreed to bring his current aids for comparison.

Dr. Susan Alvarez called on behalf of her father seeking tinnitus relief and asked about financing options for a premium pair. Agent Rosey outlined monthly financing plans and the one year of follow-up care included with each fitting. She booked a consultation and emailed the provider location details.

Dorothy Chambers, a new patient, called to schedule her first hearing evaluation after struggling to follow conversations at family dinners. Agent Lee collected her name, date of birth, phone number, and preferred clinic, then explained what to expect at the consultation and the 30-day trial. He booked her Genesis AI fitting consultation for the following week and confirmed her insurance details.

Frank Delgado asked whether the Genesis AI rechargeable models could get him through a full day of golf without swapping batteries. Agent Mary confirmed the lithium-ion charge life and the included standard charger, then answered questions about waterproofing. She scheduled a consultation so he could demo the rechargeable aids in person.

Helen Whitcomb called to check the status of her custom Signature Series order placed three weeks earlier. Agent Sue looked up the order, confirmed it was still in fabrication, and gave an estimated fitting date. Helen was reassured but wanted a follow-up call once the aids arrived.

George Pruitt called about a warranty repair after one of his aids stopped charging. Agent Mike verified the device was still under the 3-year manufacturer warranty and started a repair ticket with a prepaid shipping label. George asked how long he would be without his aids during the repair.

Nancy Foster asked about financing before committing to a premium pair for her husband. Agent Jennifer explained the monthly payment plans and the bundled care package, easing her budget concerns. Nancy decided to move forward and Jennifer scheduled a consultation at their local clinic.

Arthur Benson called frustrated that his TV streamer accessory arrived but would not pair with his aids. Agent Rose walked him through the reset steps but the device still failed to connect. She escalated to technical support and arranged a replacement shipment.

Patricia Nguyen disputed a charge on her invoice that she believed was for a cleaning already covered by her one year of care. Agent Oscar reviewed the itemized bill and found the visit fell just outside the covered window. Patricia remained unhappy and asked to speak with the billing manager.

Walter Simmons called to cancel his upcoming fitting because he found a lower price at another provider. Agent Lila offered to match the financing terms but he had already decided. She processed the cancellation and noted his feedback about pricing.

Barbara Cline called upset that her warranty claim was taking longer than promised and she had been without her aids for two weeks. Agent Lee apologized, tracked the repair, and confirmed it had shipped back that morning. Barbara said the delay had made daily life very difficult.

Donald Ferris complained that his new Edge AI aids kept dropping the Bluetooth connection during phone calls. Agent Mary tried several troubleshooting steps but the issue persisted, so she booked a follow-up service visit rather than a new fitting. Donald was clearly annoyed and questioned the reliability of the technology.

An unidentified caller reached the line after hours and left a brief voicemail asking someone to call back about a repair. No name or callback number was clearly recorded. The message rolled to voicemail with no agent available.

Eleanor Hoyt called angry about a billing statement she did not recognize and demanded an immediate refund. Agent Sue could not locate a matching account under the number provided and asked for more details, which further upset the caller. Eleanor hung up before the issue could be resolved.

prompts.question: Is the customer trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: Yes. The caller is experiencing difficulty hearing conversations at work and in group settings, and wants to explore hearing aid options to improve their communication at the office and social events.

prompts.question: What are the customer's expectations?
prompts.answer: The caller expects to learn about Starkey hearing aids, schedule a consultation with a local provider, and potentially trial a device before making a purchase commitment.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: The agent should have captured the caller's email address for appointment confirmation and follow up materials, and briefly explained which Starkey platform (Genesis AI or Edge AI) would be most suitable for the caller's specific hearing loss pattern.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Starkey Hearing. This is Marcus. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. I'm calling because I've been having a hard time hearing conversations at work and with friends. I think it might be time to look into hearing aids.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm glad you reached out. We'd love to help you. To get started, can I get your first and last name?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Sure. It's Patricia. Patricia Mendez.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Patricia, thank you. And just to confirm, you're looking at hearing aids for yourself, correct?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, that's right. I've noticed it mostly in group settings and meetings. It's frustrating.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I understand. That's actually very common, especially in noisy environments. Are you located in the United States, and what's your ZIP code so I can confirm we serve your area?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I'm in Minnesota. My ZIP is 55401. I'm in Minneapolis.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Minneapolis is in our service area. We have excellent providers there. I'd like to get your phone number so we can reach you. Can you share that?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Of course. It's ****7842.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great, thank you. And what email should I use to send appointment details and next steps?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Oh, um, I'd rather just get a call. Is that okay?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Absolutely, we can do that. Now, let's get you scheduled for a consultation. We have availability this Thursday at 10 AM or Friday at 2 PM. Which works better for you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thursday at 10 AM sounds perfect.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent, Patricia. So I have you down for a consultation appointment this Thursday, October 24th at 10 AM with one of our local providers in Minneapolis. You'll be able to explore Starkey hearing aid options and ask any questions. We'll call you at ****7842 the day before as a reminder. Sound good?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, that's great. Thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Patricia. Thank you for choosing Starkey Hearing. We look forward to seeing you Thursday morning. Take care.

callDetail.aiSummary: Patricia Mendez, a new customer in Minneapolis, called Starkey Hearing to explore hearing aid options due to difficulty hearing in group settings and work conversations. Agent Marcus Bell successfully qualified her hearing need, confirmed her service area by ZIP code, and scheduled a consultation appointment for Thursday at 10 AM with a local provider. The call did not capture Patricia's email address, and no product education on Starkey's hearing aid platforms (Genesis AI or Edge AI) was provided during the intake.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, great job maintaining a warm tone and moving Patricia through the scheduling process efficiently. Two coaching points for next time. One, when a caller declines to share an email, follow up with something like, 'I'll send a text with the appointment details and any pre-visit forms to ****7842 instead.' This ensures she has written confirmation. Two, use those few seconds before closing to mention one relevant Starkey platform, for example, 'We offer Genesis AI hearing aids with advanced noise management, which really shine in group settings like the ones you mentioned.' This plants a seed and shows we heard her specific need.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Starkey Hearing, this is Danielle. How can I help you hear better today?
highlights: Thank you for calling Starkey Hearing

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Danielle. My name is Robert Callahan and I think it's finally time I looked into hearing aids. I keep missing what my grandkids say.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm glad you reached out, Robert. That's exactly what we help with. Is this the first time you've looked into hearing aids?
highlights: first time you've looked into hearing aids

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, first time. I've never worn them before. I mostly struggle in noisy places, restaurants, family dinners, that kind of thing.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's very common. For busy, noisy settings our Genesis AI and the newer Edge AI platforms do a great job separating speech from background noise. Are you looking for something discreet, or is that less of a concern?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Discreet would be nice, but honestly what does something like that run? I want to keep it manageable, I'm on a fixed income.
highlights: what does something like that run

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Absolutely, and I want to be upfront with you. Depending on the technology level, a pair can range from around $2,500 up to $7,000. The Genesis AI 16 is a wonderful mid-tier option, and we also have financing so you can spread the cost monthly.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay. See, the place across town quoted me on some off-brand pair for a lot less, but I've heard mixed things about them.
highlights: off-brand pair for a lot less

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I understand shopping around, and I'd encourage it. One thing I'll mention is Starkey is the only major brand designed and built here in America, in Minnesota, and our aids come with a full year of follow-up care, cleanings, and adjustments included. That service piece is where a lot of the value lives.
highlights: designed and built here in America

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That's good to know. I'd want to talk it over with my wife before I commit to anything, though.
highlights: talk it over with my wife before I commit

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Of course, and there's no pressure at all. Every fitting includes a 30-day trial, so nothing is locked in. The best next step is a consultation with a provider near you, which includes a full hearing evaluation at no cost.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That sounds fair. Can you set that up? I'm over in the Eden Prairie area.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I sure can. We have a provider right in Eden Prairie with an opening this Thursday at 10 AM. Shall I book that for you and your wife?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thursday at 10 works great. Let me give you my number, it's 952-555-0143.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, I've got you and your wife booked Thursday at 10 AM in Eden Prairie, and you'll get a reminder text. Anything else I can help with, Robert?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, that covers it. Thank you, Danielle.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: My pleasure. We look forward to helping you hear your grandkids again. Take care and see you Thursday.
highlights: look forward to helping you hear

brandConversationRules: Intro and offer: Introduce yourself as Starkey Hearing's AI agent here to help build a personalized hearing aid quote, mention that many providers currently include a free online hearing test plus a 30-day risk-free trial, and ask if they would like to get started.

Qualify one question at a time: Ask the key questions one at a time, covering whether they need one aid or a pair, the preferred style (RIC, BTE, or invisible custom IIC), the technology platform or features of interest (Edge AI, Genesis AI, Signature Series, rechargeable, or Bluetooth), their timeline for treatment, and finally their ZIP code so we can confirm a provider near them.

Estimate then book: Confirm we have a provider serving their ZIP, share a preliminary price range based on the platform and style they chose, explain that a hearing specialist provides an exact quote after evaluation, propose a specific day and time for a consultation, and confirm they will receive a reminder text before the appointment with a number to call.

qaPairs.question: How much do Starkey hearing aids cost?
qaPairs.answer: Starkey hearing aids generally range from about $2,000 to $7,000 per pair depending on the platform and features you choose. A specialist gives you an exact quote at your consultation, so let's get one scheduled near you.

qaPairs.question: What is the newest Starkey hearing aid?
qaPairs.answer: Edge AI RIC RT, launched in October 2024, is the newest platform with Deep Neural Network sound processing and Edge Mode+. I can book you a consultation to try it in person.

qaPairs.question: Do you have invisible hearing aids?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, the Signature Series IIC is Starkey's tiniest hearing aid built on the Genesis AI platform for a truly discreet fit. Let's schedule a consultation so a specialist can confirm the right fit for your ears.

qaPairs.question: Are Starkey hearing aids made in America?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, Starkey is the only major brand designed and built in America at its facility in Eden Prairie, Minnesota. I would be glad to book a consultation so you can learn more.

qaPairs.question: Do Starkey hearing aids connect to my phone?
qaPairs.answer: Many models, including Edge AI and Genesis AI, offer Bluetooth streaming and work with the free My Starkey App. A specialist can show you the streaming features during a consultation.

qaPairs.question: Are there rechargeable options?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, Genesis AI and Edge AI offer lithium-ion rechargeable models that come with one standard charger. Let's set up a consultation to find the best rechargeable option for you.

qaPairs.question: Can Starkey hearing aids help with tinnitus?
qaPairs.answer: Starkey offers hearing solutions designed to help manage tinnitus, and a specialist can recommend the right approach after an evaluation. I can book that consultation for you now.

qaPairs.question: What is included in the price?
qaPairs.answer: Provider pricing typically bundles your consultation, fitting and orientation, real-ear measurements, a 30-day trial, and one year of follow-up care for adjustments, cleanings, and repairs. A specialist confirms the full details at your appointment.

qaPairs.question: Is there a free hearing test?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, you can take a free online hearing test, and your provider can perform a complete evaluation in person. Let's schedule that visit near you.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer financing?
qaPairs.answer: Many providers offer financing options to make hearing aids more affordable. A specialist can walk you through the plans available in your area at your consultation.

qaPairs.question: What is the difference between Genesis AI 24 and Genesis AI 16?
qaPairs.answer: Genesis AI 24 is the top tier with the most advanced AI-powered processing, while Genesis AI 16 is a mid-tier option with 16 channels and Edge Mode+. A specialist can help you compare them during a consultation.

qaPairs.question: How long does a battery last on the Signature Series?
qaPairs.answer: The Signature Series IIC uses a size 10 battery that lasts up to 7 days. I can book a consultation so a specialist can confirm what fits your lifestyle.

qaPairs.question: Do you sell hearing aid batteries?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, disposable zinc-air batteries in sizes 10, 13, 312, and 675 are available for non-rechargeable models. Your provider can supply them and recommend the right size at your visit.

qaPairs.question: What accessories are available?
qaPairs.answer: Starkey offers wireless accessories like a remote microphone and a TV streamer that send audio directly to your hearing aids. A specialist can demonstrate them at your consultation.

qaPairs.question: Are the hearing aids waterproof?
qaPairs.answer: Several models, including all Signature Series aids, are IP68 rated for water and dust resistance. Let's schedule a consultation to review the best option for you.

qaPairs.question: Can I use a Starkey aid with my cochlear implant?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, the Bimodal Hearing Solution pairs a Starkey aid with a cochlear implant on the opposite ear. A specialist can quote and fit this for you during a consultation.

qaPairs.question: What is Edge Mode+?
qaPairs.answer: Edge Mode+ uses AI to make speech clearer at the press of a button in challenging environments. A specialist can demonstrate it during your consultation.

qaPairs.question: Do you have hearing aids for seniors?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, Starkey offers a full range of platforms and styles suited for active listeners and quieter lifestyles alike. Let's book a consultation so a specialist can recommend the right fit.

qaPairs.question: How do I find a provider near me?
qaPairs.answer: I can help you find a Starkey provider in your area right now. Just share your ZIP code and I will get a consultation scheduled for you.

qaPairs.question: What is the My Starkey App?
qaPairs.answer: The My Starkey App is a free control center for Genesis and Edge AI hearing aids that goes beyond the onboard push-buttons. A specialist can help you set it up at your appointment.
